Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Len Jewitt, Waterloo
notes:
Len Jewitt of Waterloo spoke to the volunteer initiative that contributed to a trail between Goderich and Guelph. He elaborated on the environmental impact and designs of the Trailway project. He further expanded on the funding arrangements in place for the project, and what would be required by the Region to see the project proceed.

In reply to a question from Committee, L. Jewitt explained that the engineers working with him to analyze the project provided certain rationales for measurements within the proposal, based on consultation with Regional engineers. Relatedly, L. Jewitt clarified that while the bridge is critical, it is connected with major aspects of the project. Each existing bridge is to be at a similar distance, since other sizes may necessitate different structures.

Replying to a question from Committee, L. Jewitt indicated fundraising cannot begin until this item is approved by the Region. He clarified that there are two aspects, a tunnel and a bridge, and that the bridge is at issue in the corresponding report to Council.

items.title: PDL-GDS-24-017, Kissing Bridge Trailway – Proposed Pedestrian Bridge
notes:
This item was advanced in the agenda with unanimous consent.

Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development & Legislative  Services, introduced the report and spoke to the intricacies around renewal of the lease and funding for the project. He indicated that Regional staff have met with the engineers that L. Jewitt was dealing with to discuss and analyze design.

J. Nowak introduced his motion as it relates to the report, and emphasized the timelines associated with applying for the funding for the project. He pointed out that the motion itself does not commit the Region to funding, and instead allows the organization to move forward with fundraising.

In reply to a question from the Committee, R. Regier answered that there are outstanding questions, including timing, that need to be resolved as it relates to this project. Frank Kosa, Director, Design & Construction, added that environmental assessment requirements have been considered, including indigenous consultation. He clarified that certain work has been excluded from the cost estimates provided by his team providing the designs.

In response to a question from the Committee, Doug Spooner, Commissioner, Transportation Services, clarified that the project outlined in the report is not in the capital forecast, and there is not cost certainty at this point. R. Regier indicated that staff could bring a report outlining the legal constraints and costs.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified that the motion in itself does not require funding, but will place the project into the transportation capital plan, which will then require budgeting. The overall timing is contingent on how quickly the environmental assessment can be completed. D. Spooner further clarified that the Ministry of Environment is responsible for the assessments, and that he is unsure as to what specific changes will be coming to that process.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner further clarified the requirements for the provincial funding which has an expedited timeline. Notably, the application would need to be submitted by the Region as the leaseholder, in partnership with the Township of Wellesley. R. Regier added that with the Region being the holder of the lease, the Region will acquire liability for long term maintenance.

In response to a question from Committee, Graham Walsh, Regional Solicitor/Director, Legal Services, indicated that the lease has been renewed several times, and is now set to expire in 2027, but that such an extension would require some changes in the terminology to the agreement itself. D. Spooner further added that the reason for the expedited nature of this report is that the project does not appear in the 2018 transportation master plan, due to it not being a transportation project at its core, and is more recreational, which does not typically fall under Regional jurisdiction.

items.title: TSD-TRS-24-009, Grand River Transit - Ridership Update - Second Quarter 2024
notes:
D. Spooner introduced the report, indicating that ridership continued to grow, and outlined the overall increases to service occurring at the Region. He elaborated on the work being done by the Region, especially as it pertains to the MobilityPLUS service.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner answered that the lowest performance route statistics are calculated by boardings per hour, meaning someone getting on and off the bus. Furthermore, D. Spooner provided that presenting of information is a challenge and does not reflect cost efficiency. Staff are currently looking at the strategy, including as it relates to rural delivery systems.

In response to a question from Committee, D. Spooner indicated that provincial gas tax funding is shared across the province, and the Regional funding is based on the share of ridership.

motions.item_title: PDL-GDS-24-017, Kissing Bridge Trailway – Proposed Pedestrian Bridge
motions.text: WHEREAS the Kissing Bridge Trailway (KBT) is a 45 km component of the Goderich to Guelph Rail Trail (G2G Trail) that stretches across the northern portion of the Region from Guelph to Millbank; and WHEREAS this trail is an important Regional tourist destination with economic benefits to the Region; and WHEREAS the KBT, as a component of the G2G Trail, is jointly leased by the Province of Ontario to the County of Wellington and the Region of Waterloo for use as a recreational trail; and WHEREAS the KBT as it exists is approximately 2.5 metres wide; and WHEREAS there are two gaps in the KBT that prevent it from becoming an entirely off-road trail: 1) crossing of the Grand River near West Montrose (Woolwich Township); and 2) crossing of the Conestogo River in Wallenstein (Wellesley Township); and WHEREAS the detour route for the Conestogo River crossing in Wallenstein requires users to traverse along Line 86 utilizing the shoulder of the highway and crossing the vehicular bridge over the Conestogo River; and WHEREAS this detour route is considered very dangerous due to the high volume of traffic, including many heavy trucks, with no sidewalks or trails for safe pedestrian/cyclist use; and WHEREAS unprecedented private funding has been pledged to design and construct a new pedestrian bridge along the KBT over the Conestogo River if the project can be completed in the short term; and WHEREAS significant structural engineering and environmental approval work has already been completed for the project by engineers and environmental consultants qualified to practice in the Province of Ontario that should be used to guide detailed design work and project approvals rather than duplicating this work; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Council of the Region of Waterloo direct staff to prioritize analysis of design and construction for the Conestogo River Bridge project, utilizing previously completed engineering and environmental work to the greatest extent possible, with the intent of possible construction in 2025; and further, THAT staff be directed to work closely with partners including the KBT Steering Committee, Township of Wellesley, County of Wellington, G2G Rail Trail, and community volunteers, to present viable and reasonable design options and standards for this project, including a width of 2.4 metres, that meet Ontario Engineering standards for pedestrian bridges that may or may not meet all Region of Waterloo standards or guidelines; and further, THAT staff be directed to apply for funding for this project under the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund through the Province of Ontario, and any other applicable funding streams, to offset costs; and further, THAT staff consider utilizing external consultants or a short-term contract position to manage this project rather than an additional Full-Time Employee (FTE). And that Staff be directed to bring a report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee on November 5th to outline cost breakdowns and timelines associated with this project. And further that Staff provide a report on provincial funding on September 25th Council meeting.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the Kissing Bridge Trailway (KBT) is a 45 km component of the Goderich to Guelph Rail Trail (G2G Trail) that stretches across the northern portion of the Region from Guelph to Millbank; and

WHEREAS this trail is an important Regional tourist destination with economic benefits to the Region; and

WHEREAS the KBT, as a component of the G2G Trail, is jointly leased by the Province of Ontario to the County of Wellington and the Region of Waterloo for use as a recreational trail; and

WHEREAS the KBT as it exists is approximately 2.5 metres wide; and

WHEREAS there are two gaps in the KBT that prevent it from becoming an entirely off-road trail: 1) crossing of the Grand River near West Montrose (Woolwich Township); and 2) crossing of the Conestogo River in Wallenstein (Wellesley Township); and

WHEREAS the detour route for the Conestogo River crossing in Wallenstein requires users to traverse along Line 86 utilizing the shoulder of the highway and crossing the vehicular bridge over the Conestogo River; and

WHEREAS this detour route is considered very dangerous due to the high volume of traffic, including many heavy trucks, with no sidewalks or trails for safe pedestrian/cyclist use; and

WHEREAS unprecedented private funding has been pledged to design and construct a new pedestrian bridge along the KBT over the Conestogo River if the project can be completed in the short term; and

WHEREAS significant structural engineering and environmental approval work has already been completed for the project by engineers and environmental consultants qualified to practice in the Province of Ontario that should be used to guide detailed design work and project approvals rather than duplicating this work;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Council of the Region of Waterloo direct staff to prioritize analysis of design and construction for the Conestogo River Bridge project, utilizing previously completed engineering and environmental work to the greatest extent possible, with the intent of possible construction in 2025; and further,

THAT staff be directed to work closely with partners including the KBT Steering Committee, Township of Wellesley, County of Wellington, G2G Rail Trail, and community volunteers, to present viable and reasonable design options and standards for this project, including a width of 2.4 metres, that meet Ontario Engineering standards for pedestrian bridges that may or may not meet all Region of Waterloo standards or guidelines; and further,

THAT staff be directed to apply for funding for this project under the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund through the Province of Ontario, and any other applicable funding streams, to offset costs; and further,

THAT staff consider utilizing external consultants or a short-term contract position to manage this project rather than an additional Full-Time Employee (FTE). 

And that Staff be directed to bring a report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee on November 5th to outline cost breakdowns and timelines associated with this project.

And further that Staff provide a report on provincial funding on September 25th Council meeting.
